description:
`enum_predicate_search` currently has NO perf detector. It compiles for 3.15s
(debug, fast dev machine) for a 24-line program, which by
[[feedback_tiny_fixture_slowness_is_correctness]] is a correctness signal -- and
nothing would notice if that got worse.

## Why the old detector was removed

Its `timeout.run_secs` / `timeout.interp_secs` were deliberately held just above
the local compile time so a regression would surface as a red. A wall-clock
budget calibrated on dev hardware cannot gate CI: the runners are much slower and
run under `llvm-cov` instrumentation. It exceeded its cap on EVERY CI run of the
fz-go4.1..fz-f98.24 stack -- PRs #80, #90, #91, #92, #99, #101 -- and nobody
noticed, because from #93 to #98 the lib suite failed first and cargo's fail-fast
meant the matrix never ran at all. A tripwire that is always red is not a
tripwire.

The caps are now 20s hang backstops, documented in the fixture header as
deliberately too loose to notice a perf regression (main 120c86192).

## What to build

A work-count ceiling read from telemetry -- machine independent, and it names the
defect when it fires instead of reporting the runner.
[[feedback_minimal_job_trace_acceptance]] describes the shape: gate on the
`--log-telemetry` job trace being minimal versus expected work.

fz-xat already measured the number for this exact fixture: 2625
`callable_construction` settlements for 242 executables. That is the assertion --
a settlement/derivation ceiling per fixture, not a duration.

## Design notes

- The count must come from telemetry the compiler already emits, not a test-only
  counter ([[feedback_tests_use_production_paths]]). `DemandConeSettlement`
  (members / external_members / rounds / derivations) exists and is emitted;
  check whether it is sufficient before adding anything.
- A ceiling, not an equality: fail on a REGRESSION, and tighten as fz-xat lands
  improvements.
- Declare it in the fixture header next to `timeout.*`, where the fixture
  metadata already lives, not in a side table.
- Only fixtures with a known excess-work story need one. Do not add a ceiling to
  every fixture.

## Checks

- `enum_predicate_search` carries a work ceiling that fails if settlement volume
  regresses, and passes at HEAD.
- The ceiling is derived from emitted telemetry, with no test-only counting.
- The wall-clock overrides stay loose and stay documented as hang backstops.
- Full lib + matrix at baseline or better.

## Related

- fz-xat is the actual excess work; this is only the detector that keeps it from
  regressing further.
- fz-1iw retires overrides no longer needed at all; this is the opposite case,
  where the override stays but stops pretending to be a gate.

comments.text:
SCOPE NOTE, because a commit already carries this ticket's name.

`fz-f98.23: retire a wall-clock tripwire that was always red on CI` (main
120c86192, PR #102) landed only the RETIREMENT half -- the caps moved to 20s and
the fixture header now says plainly that they are hang backstops, deliberately
too loose to notice a perf regression.

This ticket's actual subject, the REPLACEMENT, is not done. None of its Checks
are met:

    enum_predicate_search carries a work ceiling                NOT MET
    the ceiling is derived from emitted telemetry               NOT MET
    the wall-clock overrides stay loose and documented          holds

So there is currently NO perf detector on that fixture at all. That is the gap
this ticket closes, and `git log` should not be read as closure.

title: enum_predicate_search has no perf detector: replace the retired stopwatch with a work-count ceiling
